items.label: f01-import-drops-settings
items.front: A learner imports an exported progress file whose settings object is {} (or a hand-edited file with xp as a string). Evidence: importJSON only checks that the parsed value is an object, then does { ...EMPTY(), ...parsed } (src/lib/store.js:77-82), unlike load() which deep-merges settings (line 40).
items.back: The file replaces state with defaults lost (timerOn/revealDelay become undefined) and bad types accepted, then save() persists it. Deep-merge settings like load() and validate field types before replacing state.

items.label: f02-save-swallows-quota
items.front: Storage is full (or the browser is in a private mode that rejects writes) while a learner answers questions. Evidence: save() catches the setItem error silently and still notifies every listener (src/lib/store.js:47-54).
items.back: The header XP pill and mastery bars update as if saved, but everything is lost on reload with no warning. Surface a 'progress is not being saved' state when setItem fails.

items.label: f03-shaky-split-verdict
items.front: Flash self-grade 'Shaky' sends { correct: false, grade: 1 }. Evidence: src/components/question-card.js:187; schedule() treats every grade above 0 as a successful rep (src/lib/srs.js:27-34).
items.back: The weak-spot list and mastery count the card as missed while the scheduler pushes it 1-3+ days out, so the two views disagree about the same answer. Decide one meaning for 'Shaky' and derive both records from it.

items.prompt: isDue() returns true for a missing card. Why does dueQuestions also require `state.answers[q.id]` to exist?

choices.text: Unseen questions have a due date far in the future and would never be picked anyway
Missing cards throw inside isDue, so the guard prevents a crash
The guard hides questions whose lesson has not been read yet
Without it every never-answered question would count as due, flooding spaced review with the whole unseen bank

choices: Unseen questions have a due date far in the future and would never be picked anyway
Missing cards throw inside isDue, so the guard prevents a crash
The guard hides questions whose lesson has not been read yet
Without it every never-answered question would count as due, flooding spaced review with the whole unseen bank

items.explanation: isDue(card) is `!card || card.due <= now`; spaced review should resurface what you have studied, while unseen questions belong to the learning path.

items.prompt: A learner keeps answering the same multiple-choice question correctly. Why does that card's ease factor never rise above its starting 2.5?

choices.text: Multiple-choice answers bypass the scheduler entirely and only update mastery
Ease is capped at 2.5 for every question type to keep intervals short
Auto-graded questions report grade 2 when correct, and only grade 3 adds to the ease; only flash self-grading can say 'Nailed it'
Ease only changes after a lapse, never after a correct answer

Auto-graded questions report grade 2 when correct, and only grade 3 adds to the ease; only flash self-grading can say 'Nailed it'
Ease only changes after a lapse, never after a correct answer

items.explanation: grade() calls onAnswer with grade: correct ? 2 : 0; schedule adds 0.15 ease only for grade 3 (and subtracts for grade 1).

items.prompt: The app only logs a console warning when two questions share an id, yet the content validator fails the build for it. What harm justifies the hard failure?

choices.text: Progress is keyed by question id, so the two questions would silently share one answer history and one SRS card
The second question is dropped from every view, so learners never see it
XP would be awarded twice for every correct answer to either question
The app crashes on start-up when it builds the question lookup map

choices: Progress is keyed by question id, so the two questions would silently share one answer history and one SRS card
The second question is dropped from every view, so learners never see it
XP would be awarded twice for every correct answer to either question
The app crashes on start-up when it builds the question lookup map

items.explanation: state.answers and state.cards are indexed by qid; the validator header says duplicate ids silently merge two questions' progress, which no UI shows.

items.prompt: In the lesson's profile effect, userId switches from A to B quickly and A's response arrives after B's. What stops A's data from being shown?

choices.text: Before the effect re-runs for B, A's cleanup sets ignore = true and aborts A's request, so A's late result is discarded
React cancels state updates from any promise created during a previous render
fetch resolves responses in request order, so A always arrives before B
The dependency array [userId] blocks setUser calls that use an old userId

choices: Before the effect re-runs for B, A's cleanup sets ignore = true and aborts A's request, so A's late result is discarded
React cancels state updates from any promise created during a previous render
fetch resolves responses in request order, so A always arrives before B
The dependency array [userId] blocks setUser calls that use an old userId

items.explanation: Cleanup runs before the next effect execution; the `if (!ignore) setUser(data)` guard plus controller.abort() keep only the latest response.

items.prompt: A card has reps 2, interval 6 days and ease 2.5. The learner answers 'good' (grade 2). When is it due next?

choices.text: In 12 days: good answers always double the interval
In 6 days: the interval only grows on an 'easy' answer
In 15 days: from the third rep on, the interval is multiplied by the ease (6 x 2.5)
In 7 days: each good answer adds one day to the interval

choices: In 12 days: good answers always double the interval
In 6 days: the interval only grows on an 'easy' answer
In 15 days: from the third rep on, the interval is multiplied by the ease (6 x 2.5)
In 7 days: each good answer adds one day to the interval

items.explanation: reps becomes 3, so interval = round(interval * ease * 1) = 15; grade 2 leaves ease unchanged and the result is capped at 180 days.

items.prompt: Content files never store a question's tier or board points, yet every view can read q.tier and q.points. Where do they come from, and what is the trade-off?

choices.text: index.js denormalises them onto each question at load (tier inherited from its module), so views never walk the tree but content edits must go through that loader
Each view computes them on demand from the track file, so the bank stays normalized
The validator writes them back into the content files during npm test
They are read from localStorage, so points differ per learner

Each view computes them on demand from the track file, so the bank stays normalized
The validator writes them back into the content files during npm test
They are read from localStorage, so points differ per learner

items.explanation: question.tier = question.tier ?? module.tier; question.points = tier * 100 (+100 for flash). The file header: so the quiz engine, the board and the stats page never need to walk the tree.

items.prompt: A learner with a 20-day streak answers nothing on Saturday and answers a question on Sunday. What does touchStreak set the count to?

choices.text: 0: the streak is cleared and only counts again from the next day
20: a missed day pauses the streak instead of breaking it
1: only a gap of exactly one day continues the streak, and there is no grace day
21: the streak continues because the gap is under 48 hours

choices: 0: the streak is cleared and only counts again from the next day
20: a missed day pauses the streak instead of breaking it
1: only a gap of exactly one day continues the streak, and there is no grace day
21: the streak continues because the gap is under 48 hours

items.explanation: count = gap === 1 ? count + 1 : 1; best keeps the previous maximum.

items.prompt: On a flash card the learner clicks 'Shaky' (grade 1). How do the answer statistics and the SRS card treat that same click?

choices.text: Nothing is recorded until the learner picks Solid or Nailed it
Both treat it as a success: the streak grows and the interval grows
The answer is recorded as wrong (streak reset, wrong + 1), yet the card is scheduled as a successful review with a longer interval
Both treat it as a miss: the streak resets and the card comes back in ten minutes

The answer is recorded as wrong (streak reset, wrong + 1), yet the card is scheduled as a successful review with a longer interval

items.explanation: selfGradeBtn passes correct: gradeValue >= 2 (false for 1) but grade: 1; recordAnswer resets the streak on !correct while schedule() treats any grade > 0 as a pass.

items.prompt: A short-answer question accepts `useMemo`. A learner types `I would definitely NOT reach for useMemo here`. Why is it graded correct?

choices.text: Normalization strips negations such as 'not' before comparing
Grading ignores the learner's text and marks every non-empty short answer correct
Accepted strings longer than six characters match as a substring of the normalized input, so any answer that contains the term passes
It is graded wrong; only an exact normalized match is accepted

choices: Normalization strips negations such as 'not' before comparing
Grading ignores the learner's text and marks every non-empty short answer correct
Accepted strings longer than six characters match as a substring of the normalized input, so any answer that contains the term passes
It is graded wrong; only an exact normalized match is accepted

items.explanation: matchesAnswer: given === want || (want.length > 6 && given.includes(want)). Loose matching tolerates punctuation and phrasing but cannot tell a wrong sentence that mentions the term.

items.prompt: A learner answers one question correctly, correctly again, then wrong. What does questionMastery report for it afterwards?

choices.text: 0.5, because one wrong answer removes exactly one step of the two-step streak
0, because a wrong answer resets the per-question streak and mastery is streak / 2
0.67, because mastery is the share of correct answers (2 of 3)
1, because the question was already mastered and mastery never decreases

choices: 0.5, because one wrong answer removes exactly one step of the two-step streak
0, because a wrong answer resets the per-question streak and mastery is streak / 2
0.67, because mastery is the share of correct answers (2 of 3)
1, because the question was already mastered and mastery never decreases

items.explanation: recordAnswer sets streak to 0 on a wrong answer; questionMastery is clamp(entry.streak / 2, 0, 1). The README calls this deliberately strict so the numbers stay honest.

items.prompt: A card with a 30-day interval and ease 2.5 is missed (grade 0). What does schedule() do to it?

choices.text: Keeps the interval but lowers ease, so the next good answer grows it more slowly
Deletes the card so the question is treated as unseen again
Resets reps and interval to 0, lowers ease to 2.3, and makes it due again in ten minutes
Halves the interval to 15 days and leaves ease unchanged

choices: Keeps the interval but lowers ease, so the next good answer grows it more slowly
Deletes the card so the question is treated as unseen again
Resets reps and interval to 0, lowers ease to 2.3, and makes it due again in ten minutes
Halves the interval to 15 days and leaves ease unchanged

items.explanation: grade 0: lapses += 1, reps = 0, interval = 0, ease = max(1.3, ease - 0.2), due = now + 10 minutes ('get it wrong, it comes back today').
